name: Molten Cam
description: Molten Cam is a small volcanic world dominated by a series of asymmetric supervolcanoes whose eruptions follow a cam-like pattern, each one triggering the next in a cascading sequence that circles the planet every seventy-two hours. Rivers of incandescent lava flow in channels worn deep into the basalt surface, their paths describing lobed curves like the profile of a mechanical cam. The exposed planetary core glows cherry-red through a vast equatorial rift, pulsing with the rhythm of the eruption cycle.

The toxic atmosphere is a choking blend of sulfur dioxide and volcanic ash, stained orange by the eternal firelight below. Heat radiates from every surface, and the ground trembles constantly with the subsurface movement of magma following its cam-lobe pathways. The sound is a continuous low roar punctuated by the sharp crack of cooling rock and the hiss of superheated gases escaping through fissures, a world that sounds like a furnace working at full capacity.

Despite the hellish conditions, extremophile microbial colonies thrive in the mineral-rich zones between eruption paths, feeding on chemical energy from the volcanic vents. Geological surveys have detected deposits of exotic matter concentrated along the cam-lobe lava channels, apparently formed by the extreme pressures and temperatures of the eruption cycle. The mathematical precision of the volcanic sequence has led some researchers to theorize that the planet's interior has been artificially structured, though no proof has been found.

The exotic matter deposits make Molten Cam strategically valuable despite the extreme hazards of extraction. Mining operations must time their activities to the eruption cycle, working in the narrow windows between cascading volcanic events. The cam-pattern has been stable for as long as records exist, but recent seismic data suggests a new lobe may be forming, one that would alter the cycle and potentially make current mining sites untenable while exposing entirely new deposits.
